Table

Rows and columns of related records — orders, invoices, members — with sortable headers, selectable rows, a sticky header, and a responsive mode that stacks or scrolls without ever losing its table semantics. Static content; the interactive cell grid is DataGrid.

Basic usage

Install the package:

pnpm add @design-schema/react

Import the stylesheet once for the app, then the component:

import '@design-schema/react/index.css';
import { Table } from '@design-schema/react';

Examples

4 rows

Open invoices

CustomerStatusDue date
Aster StudioOpen4202026-09-30
Bramble & CoOverdue12802026-08-15
Cedar AnalyticsOpen962026-10-04
Driftwood SupplyPaid6402026-09-01
import { Table, type TableColumn, type TableRow } from '@design-schema/react';

interface Invoice extends TableRow {
  customer: string;
  status: string;
  amount: number;
  due: string;
}

const DATA: Invoice[] = [
  { id: 'inv-1001', customer: 'Aster Studio', status: 'Open', amount: 420, due: '2026-09-30' },
  { id: 'inv-1002', customer: 'Bramble & Co', status: 'Overdue', amount: 1280, due: '2026-08-15' },
  { id: 'inv-1003', customer: 'Cedar Analytics', status: 'Open', amount: 96, due: '2026-10-04' },
  { id: 'inv-1004', customer: 'Driftwood Supply', status: 'Paid', amount: 640, due: '2026-09-01' },
];

const COLUMNS: TableColumn[] = [
  { key: 'customer', header: 'Customer', isRowHeader: true },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status' },
  {
    key: 'amount',
    header: 'Amount (USD)',
    abbr: 'Amount',
    align: 'end',
    sortable: true,
    render: (row) => `$${(row as Invoice).amount.toFixed(2)}`,
  },
  { key: 'due', header: 'Due date', hideBelow: 'prose' },
];

<Table caption="Open invoices" columns={COLUMNS} data={DATA} />
19 rows

Props

PropTypeDefaultDescriptionPlatforms
caption requiredstring—

What the table lists ("Open invoices"). Rendered as the caption and the accessible name; visually hidden with `hideCaption` when a Heading directly above already says it.

Accessibility: The <caption> (web) / aria-label on the container; never omitted.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
captionLevel2 | 3 | 42

Heading level of the caption in the page outline; its size is captionSize regardless.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
footercontent—

Content below the table: a row count, pagination, a total. Rendered in the `footer` part with the table's font.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
hideCaptionbooleanfalse

Visually hide the caption; it remains the accessible name.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
columns requiredarray { key: string; header: string; abbr?: string; align?: "start" | "end" | "center"; sortable?: boolean; width?: "auto" | "min" | "fill"; isRowHeader?: boolean; hideBelow?: "prose" | "content"; render?: (row: Row) => ReactNode }[]—

Column definitions in display order. `header` is the visible heading; `align: end` for numbers; `sortable` adds the sort button; exactly one column may be `isRowHeader` (its cells become row headers, and it is the row's name when stacked); `hideBelow` drops a column below a layout width; `render` formats the cell (a Text, Link, Meter, or Button — never raw HTML).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
data requiredarray Row[] where Row = { id: string; [key: string]: unknown }—

The rows. `id` must be stable; it is what selection and keys use.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
sortobject { column: string; direction: "ascending" | "descending" }—

Controlled sort state. The table shows it; the caller sorts the data (so server-side sorting works the same way).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
defaultSortobject { column: string; direction: "ascending" | "descending" }—

Initial sort for uncontrolled use; the table then sorts `data` itself by the column value (localeCompare for strings, numeric otherwise).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
selectablenone | single | multiplenone

Adds a first column of Checkboxes (radio-like behavior for `single`) and a select-all in the header for `multiple`. Selection is row identity, not a visual state alone.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
selectedarray string[]—

Controlled selected row ids.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
defaultSelectedarray string[]—

Initially selected ids.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
responsivestack | scrollstack

Below `layout.maxWidth.prose`: `stack` turns each row into a block with the column header repeated as a label before each value (content tables — orders, people); `scroll` keeps the columns and scrolls horizontally inside a labelled region with the row-header column sticky (data tables where columns are the point). Roles are explicit on every element so both keep table semantics.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
stickyHeaderbooleantrue

The header row stays visible while the body scrolls (the page, or `maxHeight`).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
maxHeightnone | viewportnone

`viewport` caps the table at the viewport height minus the section rhythm and scrolls the body; `none` lets the page scroll.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
densitycompact | comfortablecomfortable

Cell padding: layout.inset.sm or layout.inset.md.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
stripedbooleanfalse

Alternate row backgrounds. Useful past about eight columns; borders are the default row separator.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
emptyMessagestring—

Shown in place of the body when `data` is empty. Defaults to `copy.empty`.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
loadingbooleanfalse

Data is being fetched: the body shows `copy.loading` and aria-busy is set. Existing rows stay visible while re-sorting.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
rowActionsfunction (row: Row) => ReactNode—

Renders a trailing actions cell: Buttons (ghost, sm, iconOnly with Tooltip) or a Menu. Kept out of `columns` so the header can be a visually-hidden "Actions".

web, lit, rn, swiftui

Events

EventTypeDescriptionPlatforms
onSortChangeonSortChange / sort-change

Fired when a sortable header is activated, with `{ column, direction }` (cycling ascending → descending on the same column, ascending on a new one).

web, lit, rn, swiftui
onSelectionChangeonSelectionChange / selection-change

Fired with the new array of selected ids.

web, lit, rn, swiftui
onRowPressonRowPress / row-press

Fired when a row is activated, with its id. Only when the row has no other interactive content; the row header cell becomes a Button and the row is styled interactive. Prefer a Link in the row header for navigation.

web, lit, rn, swiftui

Accessibility

Decisions this component leaves to you

Supply an accessible name. This component has no text of its own to fall back on, so without one a screen reader announces its role and nothing else.

Required props that carry accessibility meaning: caption. Each is described in the props table above.

Implicit ARIA role: table.

Anatomy

containerscrollRegiontablecaptionheaderheaderRowcolumnHeadersortButtonbodyrowrowHeadercellselectCellselectAllCellstackedLabelemptyStatefooter

What generation guarantees

Accessible name — Every instance carries a programmatic name. Where the component has no text of its own to use, the name is a prop the consumer supplies.

Keyboard operable — Everything the pointer can do here, the keyboard can do — see the keyboard section.

Arrow navigation — Arrow keys move between items; Home and End jump to the ends.

Visible focus — Keyboard focus is always drawn, from the theme’s focus tokens, and is never removed.

Contrast — Text and meaningful non-text contrast meets WCAG AA; the pairs are listed below.

Target size — Interactive targets are at least 24×24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.2 Target Size, minimum).

Selected state — Selection is exposed programmatically (`aria-selected` / `aria-checked`).

Live region — Changes are announced through a live region, without moving focus.

No hover-only content — Nothing is reachable by hover alone; keyboard focus reveals the same content.

3 rows

Table keyboard support

KeyAction
TabMoves through interactive content in reading order: select-all, then per row the checkbox, links, buttons and the actions cell. Cells themselves are not focusable — this is a table, not a grid.
Enter or SpaceOn a sort button, sorts; on a row checkbox, toggles; on a row header button, activates the row.
ArrowRight or ArrowLeftIn `responsive: scroll` below the breakpoint, the scroll region is focusable and arrows scroll it horizontally. (scroll region focused)
